bullets.text: A family in Thirumazhisai waited two and a half hours for last rites because of a crematorium power outage, so the office should check local utility reliability.
Velachery floods persist despite 32.6 km of stormwater drains worth 47.5 crore rupees, meaning the office must review drainage effectiveness and infrastructure gaps.
Commuters in Adambakkam face hardship because trains running up to St. Thomas Mount do not stop, so the office should coordinate with railways to fix the schedule.
Over 3,000 Avadi streetlights remain non-functional despite a 22 crore rupee maintenance contract, prompting the office to demand accountability from the municipal corporation.
Auto rickshaw workers protested against the Vetri Payanam scheme citing livelihood threats, so the office should engage union leaders to review their grievances.
Cloud firm Vultr plans a 20 megawatt supercluster in Chennai, and the office should support this expansion to boost local infrastructure.
Tata Communications is investing 4,000 crore rupees for an AI fibre network across India, so the office must highlight Chennai within this digital corridor.
The Tamil Nadu government will soon launch e-Sevai 2.0 with new technology for faster public services, and the office should monitor its rollout across districts.

stories.title: 2.5-hour wait for family with body as crematorium suffers power trouble in Thirumazhisai
takeaways: A grieving family waited two and a half hours for last rites due to power failure in Thirumazhisai crematorium.
The incident highlights civic infrastructure failures in Thiruvallur district that require immediate administrative intervention.
